explanation: Magnesium reacts rapidly with dilute hydrochloric acid, releasing hydrogen gas and forming magnesium chloride.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: A shiny grey magnesium ribbon in colourless dilute hydrochloric acid.
beaker_view.final_appearance: A colourless magnesium chloride solution; the ribbon is consumed.
beaker_view.observation: The ribbon fizzes vigorously and dissolves quickly — faster and more energetically than any other common metal reacting with this acid — and the tube warms noticeably within seconds.
